title: 2007 HMMT February Geometry Problem 1
statement: A cube of edge length \(s>0\) has the property that its surface area is equal to the sum of its volume and five times its edge length. Compute all possible values of \(s\).

solutions.text:
1,5. The volume of the cube is \(s^{3}\) and its surface area is \(6 s^{2}\), so we have \(6 s^{2}=s^{3}+5 s\), or \(0=s^{3}-6 s^{2}+5 s=s(s-1)(s-5)\).
